categories.name: Target Hardware & Build Configuration
categories.description: Defines the target board, motor, driver hardware, power supply, phase outputs, and build/deployment target.
requirements: The firmware shall interface with the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 motor driver based on the STSPIN830.
The firmware shall be capable of rotating the GBM2804H-100T three-phase gimbal motor.
The firmware shall assume the motor has 7 pole pairs.
The system shall be powered by a 12 V DC supply during this test.
The motor drive outputs shall be the U, V, W three-phase outputs.
The firmware shall build successfully, be flashable to the NUCLEO-G431RB target board, and execute on that board without modification.

categories.name: Motor Driver & PWM Generation
categories.description: Implements TIM1 three-phase PWM, the STSPIN830 three-input interface, open-loop sinusoidal field generation, and configured electrical drive parameters.
requirements: The firmware shall configure TIM1 to generate three-phase PWM.
The firmware shall use the factory-default X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 three-input configuration.
The firmware shall generate a rotating three-phase electrical field using open-loop sinusoidal PWM.
STBY shall be controlled to enable and disable the motor driver.
The PWM switching frequency shall be 20 kHz.
The initial PWM amplitude shall be 10%.
The PWM amplitude shall not exceed 20% during this test.
The initial electrical frequency shall be 1 Hz.
The electrical-frequency ramp target shall be 10 Hz.
The firmware shall support clockwise and counter-clockwise rotation; issuing "DIR CW" or "DIR CCW" shall reverse the generated phase sequence and rotation direction accordingly.

categories.name: Motor Startup, Lifecycle & Fault Safety
categories.description: Owns motor initialization, startup ramping, start/stop state transitions, PWM shutdown behavior, and STSPIN830 fault handling.
requirements: The startup sequence shall start with a low PWM amplitude.
The startup sequence shall gradually ramp the electrical frequency from its initial value toward the target.
MOTOR START shall not be blocked because ADC measurements, motor electrical parameters, characterization, FOC, observer, current sensing, or closed-loop control are unavailable.
MOTOR START shall depend only on successful PWM/GPIO initialization and the absence of an active STSPIN830 hardware fault.

On reset or power-up, the firmware shall hold the motor driver in standby (disabled) via STBY until TIM1/GPIO are fully configured and PWM outputs are in a defined inactive state; only then may the driver be enabled.

When PWM is disabled (by MOTOR STOP or driver fault), the three driver input pins shall be driven to the documented inactive level for the factory three-input configuration, ensuring no residual drive is applied to the motor phases.
After boot/reset and before any command is issued, PWM shall remain disabled and the motor shall remain stopped.
Upon receiving the UART command "MOTOR START", the firmware shall initiate the defined open-loop startup ramp.
Upon receiving the UART command "MOTOR STOP", the firmware shall immediately disable PWM (within one control cycle) and stop the motor.
An active STSPIN830 EN/FAULT condition shall immediately disable PWM (within one control cycle).

categories.name: UART Command & Status Interface
categories.description: Provides the fixed UART protocol, command parsing and validation, direction/frequency/duty controls, error handling, and status responses.
requirements: Upon receiving the UART command "DIR CW", the firmware shall set the rotation direction to clockwise.
Upon receiving the UART command "DIR CCW", the firmware shall set the rotation direction to counter-clockwise.
Upon receiving the UART command "FREQ <Hz>", the firmware shall set the electrical frequency to the specified value.
Upon receiving the UART command "DUTY <%>", the firmware shall set the PWM amplitude to the specified value within the configured safe limit.
The STATUS response shall include the current motor state.
The STATUS response shall include the current rotation direction.
The STATUS response shall include the current electrical frequency.
The STATUS response shall include the current PWM duty.
The STATUS response shall include the driver fault status.
The firmware shall accept UART commands to set rotation direction using "DIR CW" and "DIR CCW".

The firmware shall specify and use a fixed UART configuration (port, baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, and command delimiter) for the command interface so that the listed commands can be reliably exchanged.
The firmware shall reject any unknown UART command with an explicit error response and shall not change motor state or configuration as a result of an unrecognized command.

The firmware shall validate the FREQ command argument and reject non-numeric, missing, or negative values with an error response; the electrical-frequency setpoint shall remain unchanged on rejection.
The firmware shall validate the DUTY command argument and reject non-numeric, missing, or negative values with an error response; the PWM duty setting shall remain unchanged on rejection.

Upon receiving the UART command "STATUS", the firmware shall return a response within a reasonable time containing the current motor state, rotation direction, electrical frequency (Hz), PWM duty (%), and driver fault status.

categories.name: Open-Loop Demonstration Scope & Validation
categories.description: Captures the basic-rotation demonstration objective and the explicit limitations and exclusions of the open-loop firmware.
requirements: MOTOR START shall produce visible motor movement or rotation.
The firmware shall demonstrate basic rotation to verify the MCU board, motor-driver board, PWM outputs, and motor connections.
Electrical frequency shall be used solely to create a rotating field and not as a closed-loop RPM setpoint.
The firmware shall not measure or guarantee actual mechanical RPM.

The firmware shall not implement the following features: Sensorless FOC; Motor resistance, inductance or flux characterization; Rotor observer; Clarke/Park and inverse transforms; Current PI or speed PI controller; Closed-loop RPM control; Phase-current ADC control; VBUS ADC control; ADC-triggered DMA; Current-offset calibration; Oscilloscope integration; Automatic motor-parameter identification.
